source_ref: Latifi A et al. (2026) 'Development and psychometric validation of the insect fear questionnaire for school-aged children in Iran', PLOS ONE, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0344126 (CC BY 4.0) -- S1 Table 'Questionnaire for assessing Insect phobia in Iranian children-aged group', doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0344126.s001 (DOCX, cached .cache/latifi_2026_insect_fear/s001.docx, read with python-docx); S1 Dataset (article s002) SPSS deposit doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0344126.s002 (cached .cache/latifi_2026_insect_fear/s002.sav, variable and value labels read with pyreadstat); article Methods 'Item generation' and Results 'Age- and gender-related analyses'; processing script data/latifi_2026_insect_fear.py
note: Item and option wording transcribed from S1 Table (DOCX supplement) of Latifi et al. (2026) PLOS ONE, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0344126 (CC BY 4.0), which prints all 32 items prefixed with the very codes the live data uses (Q1..Q32). RESP DIRECTION OVERRIDE, deliberate: the shipped anchors for Q1-Q23 are REVERSED relative to the SPSS deposit's own value labels. The deposit (s002.sav) labels Q1-Q23 1='completly disagree'..5='completly agree' and Q24-Q32 1='Never'..5='Always'; the paper's Methods instead says 'knowledge and entomophobia: 1 = Strongly disagree to 5 = Strongly agree. Pesticide use and personal anxiety: 1 = Always to 5 = Never', i.e. it says the FREQUENCY block is the reversed one. The two sources cannot both be right and the data says both are wrong about which block reverses: the paper's own reported age correlations reproduce from the live table only if the AGREEMENT block is the reversed one (published knowledge r=0.10 / insectophobia r=0.035 / anxiety r=0.077 against observed +0.100 / +0.034 / +0.074 under the shipped orientation; the deposit's labelled direction gives -0.100 and -0.034 for the first two). Corroborated by Q26 'I use insecticides at school' (77.2% at resp=1) and Q27 'I have insecticide with me' (89.2% at resp=1), which fixes resp 1 = Never for the frequency block, and by cor(anxiety, insectophobia) = +0.442 and girls > boys on insectophobia (3.41 vs 2.97) under the shipped orientation, both of which invert under the labelled direction. So Q1-Q23 ship as 1=Strongly agree..5=Strongly disagree and Q24-Q32 as 1=Never..5=Always. Anchor wording is S1 Table's ('Strongly disagree','Disagree','No Idea','Agree','Strongly agree' / 'Never','Rarely','Sometimes','Often','Always'), not the deposit's typo-laden value labels ('completly disagree','no idia'), and 'No Idea' keeps S1's casing. MAPPING (item axis): data/latifi_2026_insect_fear.py melts source columns Q1..Q32 by name with no rename (item_cols = [f'Q{i}' for i in range(1, 33)]), so the IRW code IS the .sav column name, and S1 Table labels each item with that same code -- a label match on all 32, code-derivation pattern 1. LANGUAGE: administered to schoolchildren in East Azerbaijan Province, Iran; the article never names the administration language but describes the instrument as the Persian one ('no validated Persian instrument exists for measuring insect-related fear'), so language=Persian. No Persian wording exists in scope -- S1 Table is English only and s002.sav has zero Persian characters across its column names, variable labels (all NULL bar Q30's '.') and value labels -- so the fallback applies: the study's own English in the base fields, _translated empty. STEP 3b: clean; 32 items on 1-5 matches the questionnaire exactly, and there is no other instrument in this study. INSTRUCTIONS/SECTIONS: S1 Table prints no instructions and no passage/testlet grouping, so instructions and section_prompt are blank and section_id is the trivial latifi_2026_insect_fear_1; the four subscale headings (Knowledge Q1-4, Entomophobia Q5-23, Behavior Q24-27, Personal fear and Anxiety Q28-32) are column headers in the source, not prompts, and were not invented into section_prompt. RIGHTS: no block. The instrument is the authors' own researcher-made questionnaire, first published in this CC BY 4.0 article and its CC BY 4.0 supplement; no fee, no redistribution clause and no use restriction was found from any rights holder.
public_note: The response scale shipped for items Q1-Q23 runs 1 = Strongly agree to 5 = Strongly disagree, which is the OPPOSITE of the direction stated by both the study's SPSS deposit's value labels and its Methods section; the data forces it. Under the direction shipped here the paper's own published age correlations reproduce from the IRW table almost exactly (knowledge 0.100 vs published 0.10, insectophobia 0.034 vs 0.035, anxiety 0.074 vs 0.077), whereas the labelled direction flips the sign of the first two, makes general anxiety correlate -0.44 with insect fear, and puts boys above girls on insect fear. Items Q24-Q32 run 1 = Never to 5 = Always as labelled. The wording itself is the study's own English questionnaire (S1 Table); the children answered a Persian version that the article does not publish

source_ref: Lee SJ, Cloninger CR, Chae H (2024) PeerJ 12:e18379, doi:10.7717/peerj.18379 (CC BY 4.0), PMC11566513; supplements peerj-12-18379-s002.xlsx (data, bare headers SWLS1..SWLS5) and peerj-12-18379-s001.doc (STROBE checklist), via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint; published Table 2 by-sex SWLS totals and Methods alpha; wording from SWLS_English.doc at labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/Documents/SWLS_English.doc (Diener, Emmons, Larsen & Griffin 1985); data/lee_2024_cloninger.py
note: MAPPING: item codes SWLS1..SWLS5 ARE the source column names -- data/lee_2024_cloninger.py selects them from the deposit workbook by prefix ([c for c in df.columns if c.startswith('SWLS')]) and melts BY NAME, so there is no positional or generated code and no rename step to get wrong. But nothing in the deposit ties those codes to text: peerj-12-18379-s002.xlsx Sheet1 has a single bare header row (ID, age, sex, i1..i140, SWLS1..SWLS5, PANAS1..PANAS20, Social Support_01..25, Subjective health), Sheet2 is empty, there are no variable or value labels (it is .xlsx, not .sav), the other supplement (peerj-12-18379-s001.doc) is a STROBE checklist, and the paper reproduces no items. Mapping SWLS-N -> canonical SWLS item N is therefore reconstructed from the numeric suffix plus the instrument's published item order. Checked against the data (verify_lee_2024_swls.R): route 3 reproduces the paper's Table 2 by-sex totals exactly (males n=195 21.89+/-5.85 published vs 21.89+/-5.85 live; females n=332 20.59+/-6.34 vs 20.60+/-6.34) and alpha .86 vs .857, which pins scale membership, raw (unreversed) storage and the 1=disagree..7=agree direction (the flipped reading gives a male mean of 18.11, off by 3.78); route 7/8 pins SWLS5, which carries both the lowest mean (3.816) and the largest SD (1.786), the SWLS literature's signature of item 5, and that also rejects the one rival hypothesis the item-total pattern raises. SWLS1..SWLS4 are NOT separated from one another by any available route, so PARTIAL, not VERIFIED. HONEST DISCREPANCY: Diener et al. (1985) report item 5 as the weakest item (loading .61 vs .72-.84), but here the lowest corrected item-total is SWLS2 (.548) with SWLS5 mid-pack (.680); under a SWLS2<->SWLS5 swap canonical item 5 ('I would change almost nothing') would carry the scale's highest mean (4.670), which no SWLS sample shows, so this is read as a sample-level finding rather than a mapping defect. TEXT: transcribed verbatim from Diener's official SWLS_English.doc (labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/Documents/SWLS_English.doc, linked from labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/SWLS.html, fetched 2026-09-08), including its instructions and its seven anchor labels; that document's scoring bands (31-35 Extremely satisfied, etc.) are not item text and were not shipped. LANGUAGE: the paper states 'We used the version of SWLS translated into Korean by Lee (2004)' and the sample is a Korean community sample, so administration was Korean. Neither supplement nor the paper contains a single Hangul character (checked: 0 CJK/Hangul characters in the PMC full text and no text columns in the workbook), so the English original ships in the base fields with the _translated columns empty -- the documented translated_substitute fallback, language=Korean retained per the standard. ANCHOR DIVERGENCE: the paper describes its 7-point scale as 'ranging from not at all (1) to extremely true (7)', which is not the SWLS's own Strongly disagree..Strongly agree wording that ships here; the paper gives only those two endpoints in English gloss, so the canonical seven labels were shipped and the divergence is disclosed in the public_note rather than papered over. RIGHTS: wording taken from labs.psychology.illinois.edu/~ediener/Documents/SWLS_English.doc; that page's only stated term is permissive -- 'The scale is copyrighted but you are free to use it without permission or charge by all professionals (researchers and practitioners) as long as you give credit to the authors of the scale: Ed Diener, Robert A. Emmons, Randy J. Larsen and Sharon Griffin'. eddiener.com/satisfaction-with-life-scale-swls/ does carry 'The use of this scale is permitted for non-commercial purposes only.' (retrieved 2026-09-08), but it was NOT used as the wording source, so under Ben's 2026-09-04 ruling (the terms of the page actually copied from govern) its clause does not apply -- same call as extremera_2016_swls (batch_031) and dudasova_2021_swls (batch_028). The conflict between the two Diener pages is unresolved corpus-wide and is flagged in batch_028/provenance.csv (duboz_2021_swls). INSTRUMENT CHECK (Step 3b): live data is 5 items on 1-7, matching the paper's 'The SWLS includes 5 items with a 7-point Likert scale'; the deposit's other three instruments (TCI i1-i140 on 0-4, PANAS on 1-5, Social Support on 1-5) are separate IRW tables and are not touched here.
public_note: The SWLS was administered in Korean (the Lee 2004 translation), but neither the PeerJ paper nor its supplements reproduce any Korean wording -- the deposit workbook carries bare column headers and no variable labels -- so the item text shown is the original English SWLS from the instrument's own distribution page and is not what respondents read. Two further caveats: the shipped seven anchors are the SWLS's own Strongly disagree..Strongly agree labels, whereas the paper describes its 7-point scale as running from 'not at all (1)' to 'extremely true (7)', and the shipped instructions describe a self-completed paper form ('placing the appropriate number on the line preceding that item'); and which canonical SWLS item corresponds to SWLS1..SWLS4 rests on the source column numbering rather than on any published item-level statistic (SWLS5 is pinned independently by having both the lowest mean, 3.82, and the largest SD, 1.79)
